$comment: Every skill in .claude/skills/, and for one copied from somewhere else, where it came from. `task skills:check` holds the directory to this file; `task skills:fetch` makes the copies match it; `task skills:add -- <name>` adds one. owner 'template' is in every API built on the template; owner 'api' was added for this API. A skill with no source is written here and maintained by hand. integrations: what this API calls or is called by, each { name, skill (a name above, or null), note }, recorded by /write-spec so the question is asked once.

skills.name: write-spec
skills.for: Writing and changing the spec with the user: the contract and the feature files

skills.name: implement-api
skills.for: Implementing the API from the spec until task ci is green

skills.name: aws-emulator
skills.for: The local stack: starting AWS Emulator, connection, certificate and signing errors, and whether an AWS operation is expected to work on it

skills.name: aws-serverless
skills.for: Lambda and API Gateway: how the function and the HTTP API behave and are configured

skills.name: aws-sdk-js-v3-usage
skills.for: Calling AWS from the function with the AWS SDK for JavaScript v3

skills.name: aws-iam
skills.for: The function's role and the deploy role: policies that grant what is used and no more

offered.name: amazon-dynamodb
offered.for: Designing the data layer in src/store/: access patterns, keys and indexes
offered.when: The API stores its data in DynamoDB, the template's default, and has more than a few access patterns

offered.name: aws-observability
offered.for: Alarms, dashboards, logs and tracing beyond the template's standard alarms
offered.when: The API is going to production and someone will be on call for it

offered.name: amazon-eventbridge-event-bus
offered.for: The new EventBridge custom event bus: subscribers, ordered delivery, deduplication, retention and replay, CloudEvents published as they are
offered.when: The API's events are to move from the classic bus the template builds to the new bus, or a subscriber is being built on one
